subject: SLA addendum: monthly credit cap & uptime banding proposal
message_1_subject: SLA addendum and monthly credit cap
message_1_body:
Hi Laura and team,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement at Optimus Data has reviewed Redwood’s standard SLA and we're close, but there are two sticking points for legal: the uptime floor and the potential size of monthly service credits.

Specifically, our procurement policy prefers a 99.90% uptime floor for hosted services with a hard cap on monthly credits at 30% of the invoiced month for the Tier-1 environment. Redwood’s standard template looks to us like it can result in larger exposure (we saw examples with >50% credits in rare severe outages). That exposure is blocking our SOW approval.

Can we get an addendum that:
- Limits monthly credits to 30% for the production environment (we can discuss higher tiers for staging)
- Clarifies uptime banding and defines per-incident credit caps (we want to avoid a single incident triggering the full monthly cap)

If you can share a redline version that shows the credit cap and the per-incident carveouts, procurement will move forward quickly. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Reed
VP Procurement, Optimus Data
daniel.reed@optimusdata.com
+1 415-555-0192
message_2_subject: Re: SLA addendum and monthly credit cap
message_2_body:
Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. Attaching a working redline (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v3.pdf) that:
- Keeps Redwood baseline uptime at 99.95% (we believe this aligns with our hosted platform economics)
- Adds an alternate schedule that caps monthly credits at 30% for the customer’s designated production tenant (we’ve called out Optimus Data Prod in the addendum)
- Adds a per-incident cap equal to 15% of the monthly invoice (so one incident can’t take the full cap)

Two quick notes:
1) To keep the 99.95% baseline without re-pricing across customers, the addendum includes a limited carveout window for scheduled maintenance and certain third-party provider events.
2) For tighter SLOs (99.99% or lower credit exposure) we can offer Dedicated pools or a higher commitment tier — happy to include an appendix with pricing options if you want to explore that route.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached redline and mark any clause you need changed.
- If procurement is comfortable with 30%/15% model, we can prepare a Docusign addendum and loop legal.

I’ve cc’d Karthik and Jonas for technical & legal wording.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v3.pdf
message_3_subject: Re: SLA addendum and monthly credit cap
message_3_body:
Laura —

Thanks for the redline. A few comments after procurement/legal review:
- The 30% monthly cap is reasonable, but legal insists that certain large incidents can’t be double-counted across multiple clauses (we’d like language that prevents compounding credits across overlapping definitions).
- We also need a 99th percentile latency objective for API tail latency (p99 < 450ms for the generation endpoint) included in the service table — if you can surface an operational metric we can hold to, that helps our SRE acceptance testing.
- Lastly, is there a way to specify a per-incident SLA investigation timeline (e.g., initial incident response within 1 hour, root-cause ETA within 72 hours)?

If you can incorporate those items we can sign quickly. Can we aim to have a final redline by EOD Monday?

Regards,
Daniel
Daniel Reed
VP Procurement, Optimus Data
message_4_subject: Internal: redline guidance for Optimus — per-incident caps + latency SLO
message_4_body:
Team —

Summary of proposed changes to include in the next redline (technical perspective):
- Add explicit "per-incident credit cap" of 15% of monthly invoice, and a clause preventing stacking of credits for a single root cause event (sample text in the attached internal doc).
- Define latency SLO for generation API: p95 < 180ms, p99 < 450ms measured at Redwood's edge for production tenant; include measurement window and sample-rate (1 min buckets, 1% sampled requests for full-trace debugging).
- Incident timelines: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour of detection, status updates every 4 hours until remediation, RCA delivered within 72 hours or preliminary RCA in 72 hours with full report in 10 business days.
- Call out an optional "priority processing" add-on (Dedicated queue) to achieve p99 < 150ms — pricing appendix to follow if customer prefers lower latency rather than larger credit exposure.

I recommend we accept the 30% monthly cap but include the technical limits above and the non-compounding language requested by legal. Laura — if you want I can draft the exact clause for "non-compounding credits" and the latency measurement appendix this afternoon.

Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
message_5_subject: Final redline: SLA addendum with credit caps & latency appendix
message_5_body:
Daniel —

Thanks for the precise feedback. Attached is a final redline (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v3_redlines.pdf) that incorporates:
- Monthly credit cap for Optimus Data Prod = 30% of the monthly invoice.
- Per-incident cap = 15% of the monthly invoice and explicit non-compounding language so overlapping definitions do not multiply credit exposure.
- Latency objectives added to the Service Table: p95 < 180ms, p99 < 450ms for the production tenant (measurement details in Appendix A).
- Incident timelines: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour, status cadence every 4 hours, preliminary RCA within 72 hours.
- Appendix B: Dedicated/priority processing pricing note if Optimus wants tighter latency (p99 < 150ms).

If this looks good, I’ve started a DocuSign flow (link below) so we can get legal sign-off asap. If you prefer a short call to confirm the measurement language, I’m available tomorrow 10–11am PT.
